 Hon'Ble Subhash Vidyarthi, J. 
1.

Heard Sri Shankar Lal Pandey, the learned counsel for the applicant as well as Smt. Shikha Sinha,
the learned Additional Government Advocate appearing on behalf of the State and perused the records.

2. The instant application has been filed by the applicant seeking anticipatory bail in F.I.R. bearing Case Crime No.245 of 2018, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 409, 406 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Fatanpur, District Pratapgarh.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an F.I.R. lodged on 30.12.2018 against five persons, including the applicant, stating that payments were released for construction of latrines under Pradhanmantri Gramin Awas Yojna without actual construction thereof.

Regarding the applicant it is stated in the F.I.R. that the applicant is a computer operator and he had uploaded some documents without the signatures of Gram Pradhan and Secretary of Gram Panchayat Sachiv.

4. In the affidavit filed in support of the anticipatory bail-application it has been contended that the applicant is innocent, he has no criminal history and he has falsely been implicated in the present case.

It has also been submitted on behalf of the applicant that the co-accused Bhola Pal has already been granted anticipatory bail by this court by means of an order dated 13.08.2025, passed in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.883 of 2025.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application No.883 of 2025
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 5. The learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and he has submitted that the applicant is a public servant and he has committed the offence by processing payments under a government scheme without actual constructions having been carried out.
6. The substantive allegation in the present case is of processing and making payments for construction of latrines without actual constructions thereof.
Even as per the F.I.R. allegations the applicant is a computer operator.
He was not responsible for making any spot inspection for verification of construction works and the only allegation against him is that he was responsible for uploading the documents.

7. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the applicant is a government servant coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and co-accused Bhola Pal has already been granted anticipatory bail by this court and without making any observations which may affect the outcome of the case, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts are sufficient for making out a case for granting anticipatory bail to the applicant.
8. In view of the above, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.
